claim: TbAQP2 and TbAQP3 genes are arranged as a tandem pair on chromosome 10 in T. brucei.
source: In T. brucei, the AQP2 and AQP3 genes are arranged as a tandem pair on chromosome 10 and have 74% amino acid identity.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript text describing the genomic organization of these genes.

claim: TbAQP2 and TbAQP3 have 74% amino acid identity.
source: In T. brucei, the AQP2 and AQP3 genes are arranged as a tandem pair on chromosome 10 and have 74% amino acid identity.
evidence: This is a direct statement providing a quantitative measure of sequence similarity.

claim: TbAQP2 mediates pentamidine uptake.
source: Whereas TbAQP2 clearly mediates pentamidine uptake, TbAQP3 does not (Baker et al., 2012; Munday et al., 2014), nor do various chimeric AQP2/3 rearrangements that give rise to pentamidine resistance (Munday et al., 2014; Graf et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and is presented as an established fact.

claim: TbAQP3 does not mediate pentamidine uptake.
source: Whereas TbAQP2 clearly mediates pentamidine uptake, TbAQP3 does not (Baker et al., 2012; Munday et al., 2014), nor do various chimeric AQP2/3 rearrangements that give rise to pentamidine resistance (Munday et al., 2014; Graf et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Chimeric AQP2/3 rearrangements give rise to pentamidine resistance.
source: Whereas TbAQP2 clearly mediates pentamidine uptake, TbAQP3 does not (Baker et al., 2012; Munday et al., 2014), nor do various chimeric AQP2/3 rearrangements that give rise to pentamidine resistance (Munday et al., 2014; Graf et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is a single aquaporin in T. vivax and T. congolense.
source: The number of aquaporin genes varies: there is a single aquaporin in T. vivax and T. congolense, two in T. suis and three in T. brucei and its derivatives and the most probable tree (Figure 1) is consistent with the evolutionary history of the four species (Hutchinson and Gibson, 2015), and indicates AQP1 as the ancestral AQP present in all trypanosome species.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the number of aquaporin genes in these species, supported by phylogenetic analysis.

claim: There are two aquaporins in T. suis.
source: The number of aquaporin genes varies: there is a single aquaporin in T. vivax and T. congolense, two in T. suis and three in T. brucei and its derivatives and the most probable tree (Figure 1) is consistent with the evolutionary history of the four species (Hutchinson and Gibson, 2015), and indicates AQP1 as the ancestral AQP present in all trypanosome species.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the number of aquaporin genes in T. suis.

claim: There are three aquaporins in T. brucei and its derivatives.
source: The number of aquaporin genes varies: there is a single aquaporin in T. vivax and T. congolense, two in T. suis and three in T. brucei and its derivatives and the most probable tree (Figure 1) is consistent with the evolutionary history of the four species (Hutchinson and Gibson, 2015), and indicates AQP1 as the ancestral AQP present in all trypanosome species.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the number of aquaporin genes in T. brucei.

claim: AQP1 is the ancestral AQP present in all trypanosome species.
source: The number of aquaporin genes varies: there is a single aquaporin in T. vivax and T. congolense, two in T. suis and three in T. brucei and its derivatives and the most probable tree (Figure 1) is consistent with the evolutionary history of the four species (Hutchinson and Gibson, 2015), and indicates AQP1 as the ancestral AQP present in all trypanosome species.
evidence: This claim is based on phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1 and cited literature.

claim: Classical NPA/NPA and ar/R AQP selectivity filter elements are present in all AQPs except T. brucei AQP2.
source: Multiple alignment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) shows that the classical NPA/NPA and ar/R AQP selectivity filter elements are present in all AQPs except T. brucei AQP2.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence alignment data shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: For T. brucei aligned with T. suis AQP1, dN/dS is 0.21.
source: For T. brucei aligned with T. suis AQP1, dN/dS is 0.21 and for AQP3, dN/dS is 0.30 indicating purifying selection.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from phylogenetic analysis.

claim: For T. brucei AQP3 aligned with T. suis, dN/dS is 0.30 indicating purifying selection.
source: For T. brucei aligned with T. suis AQP1, dN/dS is 0.21 and for AQP3, dN/dS is 0.30 indicating purifying selection.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from phylogenetic analysis with interpretation.

claim: Comparing T. brucei AQP2 with T. brucei AQP3, dN/dS is 2.0 indicating strong selection pressure for divergence on AQP2 towards an aquaporin with increased pore size.
source: However, comparing T. brucei AQP2 with T. brucei AQP3, dN/dS is 2.0 indicating strong selection pressure for divergence on AQP2 towards an aquaporin with increased pore size.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement with interpretation about positive selection.

claim: TbAQP2S131P/S263A mutant reduced [3H]-pentamidine uptake to 4.40 ± 0.71% of the rate in the control line expressing TbAQP2WT.
source: In this cell line, uptake of 30 nM [3H]-pentamidine was reduced to 4.40 ± 0.71% (n = 4) of the rate in the control line expressing TbAQP2WT (p<0.05, Student's unpaired t-test), as well as significantly different from the rate measured in parallel in the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells (p<0.01) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from transport assays with statistical analysis.

claim: TbAQP2S131P/S263A cells are significantly sensitised to pentamidine compared to tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells.
source: The remaining pentamidine uptake was sufficient to strongly sensitise the TbAQP2S131P/S263A cells to pentamidine in a standard protocol of 48 hr incubation with the drug followed by a further 24 hr in the presence of the resazurin indicator dye (p<0.0001 vs tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null) but the EC50 was still significantly higher than the TbAQP2WT control (p<0.05) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on drug sensitivity assays with statistical analysis.

claim: TbAQP2S131P/S263A cells have a significantly higher pentamidine EC50 than TbAQP2WT control cells.
source: The remaining pentamidine uptake was sufficient to strongly sensitise the TbAQP2S131P/S263A cells to pentamidine in a standard protocol of 48 hr incubation with the drug followed by a further 24 hr in the presence of the resazurin indicator dye (p<0.0001 vs tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null) but the EC50 was still significantly higher than the TbAQP2WT control (p<0.05) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on drug sensitivity assays with statistical analysis.

claim: TbAQP2L258Y mutant reduced [3H]-pentamidine transport rate to 6.6 ± 1.4% of TbAQP2WT.
source: The mutant L258Y, which has the AQP3 Tyr-250 half of the highly conserved aromatic/arginine (ar/R) motif, responsible for pore restriction and proton exclusion (Wu et al., 2009), introduced into the TbAQP2 pore, yielded a drug transport phenotype similar to TbAQP2S131P/S263A. The [3H]-pentamidine transport rate was reduced to 6.6 ± 1.4% of TbAQP2WT (p<0.05) but remained above the rate in the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells (p<0.01) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from transport assays with statistical analysis.

claim: Cell lines expressing mutations AQP2I110W and AQP2L264R, either alone or in combination, displayed pentamidine transport rates not significantly different from the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null controls.
source: Cell lines expressing mutations AQP2I110W and AQP2L264R, either alone or in combination, displayed pentamidine transport rates, and pentamidine and cymelarsan EC50 values that were not significantly different from the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null controls but highly significantly different from the TbAQP2WT drug-sensitive controls, showing that their capacity for pentamidine and cymelarsan uptake had been reduced to zero (Figure 2A,D–F).
evidence: This is based on transport assays and drug sensitivity tests with statistical analysis.

claim: The unique TbAQP2 replacement of the NPA/NPA motif and all of the WGYR selectivity filter mutations are necessary for the observed pentamidine and melaminophenyl arsenical sensitivity.
source: We conclude that the unique TbAQP2 replacement of the NPA/NPA motif and all of the WGYR selectivity filter mutations are necessary for the observed pentamidine and melaminophenyl arsenical sensitivity observed in cells expressing wild-type TbAQP2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutational analysis data presented.

claim: TbAQP3W102I/R256L/Y250L accumulated significantly more [3H]-pentamidine than the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells.
source: However, by measuring [3H]-pentamidine uptake over 30 min it was possible to reliably and reproducibly measure radiolabel accumulation in each cell line. This showed that while uptake in TbAQP3W102I/R256L only trended slightly upwards (p>0.05), the mutant AQP3 with all three AQP2 WGYR residues (W102I, R256L and Y250L) accumulated significantly more [3H]-pentamidine than the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells (p<0.01) or the null cells expressing TbAQP3WT (p=0.011).
evidence: This is based on transport assays with statistical analysis.

claim: Only TbAQP3W102I/R256L/Y250L conveyed significant sensitisation to pentamidine in tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells.
source: This is further corroborated by comparing the pentamidine sensitivity profile of these cell lines: only TbAQP3W102I/R256L/Y250L conveyed significant sensitisation to tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells (p<0.0001; Figure 2H).
evidence: This is based on drug sensitivity assays with statistical analysis.

claim: TbAQP3 is converted into a pentamidine transporter by the insertion of the AQP2 WGYR residues.
source: Thus, TbAQP3 is converted into a pentamidine transporter by the insertion of the AQP2 WGYR residues, although this does not convey as high a rate of pentamidine uptake as TbAQP2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutational analysis and transport data.

claim: TbAQP2I190T displayed dramatically reduced [3H]-pentamidine uptake at 2.7 ± 0.7% of the TbAQP2WT control.
source: TbAQP2I190T displayed dramatically reduced [3H]-pentamidine uptake, at 2.7 ± 0.7% (p<0.01, n = 4) of the TbAQP2WT control, although significantly higher than the rate of the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null negative control (p<0.05) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from transport assays with statistical analysis.

claim: The reduced pentamidine uptake rate in TbAQP2I190T was the result of a reduced Vmax of the high affinity [3H]-pentamidine uptake, rather than a change in Km.
source: The reduced rate was the result of a reduced Vmax of the high affinity [3H]-pentamidine uptake, rather than a change in Km; the LAPT1 Vmax and Km were unchanged in cells expressing TbAQP2I190T or TbAQP2WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on kinetic analysis of transport data.

claim: TbAQP2I190T/W192G displayed no significant pentamidine uptake above tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null.
source: Substitution W192G also produced intermediate sensitivity to both drugs (Figure 3C) but the double substitution TbAQP2I190T/W192G displayed no significant pentamidine uptake above tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null (Figure 3A) and did not sensitise to pentamidine or cymelarsan (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is based on transport assays and drug sensitivity tests.

claim: Each of the L-to-W mutants (L84W, L118W, L218W) exhibited significantly reduced pentamidine sensitivity compared to TbAQP2WT.
source: Expressing each of the L-to-W mutants in tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells revealed significantly reduced pentamidine sensitivity compared to the same cells expressing TbAQP2WT (Figure 4A), while also exhibiting dramatically reduced rates of [3H]-pentamidine transport (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on drug sensitivity assays and transport measurements.

claim: TbAQP2L84W/L118W did not significantly sensitise for pentamidine and displayed no detectable increase in [3H]-pentamidine transport relative to tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells.
source: This effect was additive, with TbAQP2L84W/L118W not significantly sensitising for pentamidine and displaying no detectable increase in [3H]-pentamidine transport relative to tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null cells (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is based on drug sensitivity assays and transport measurements.

claim: L84M and L218M variants were not or barely different from TbAQP2WT with respect to pentamidine sensitisation.
source: When the same leucine residues were replaced with methionine instead of tryptophan, variants L84M and L218M were not or barely different from TbAQP2WT with respect to pentamidine sensitisation (Figure 4A) or transport (but highly significantly different from their respective tryptophan variants).
evidence: This is based on drug sensitivity assays and transport measurements with comparisons.

claim: All of the position 84, 118 and 218 Trp and Met mutants were able to transport glycerol.
source: By this measure, all of the position 84, 118 and 218 Trp and Met mutants were able to transport glycerol, as each displayed SHAM EC50 values significantly different from the tbaqp1-2-3 null cells (Figure 4C,D); several variants displayed an intermediate SHAM EC50, being also significantly different from TbAQP2WT, indicating some attenuation of glycerol efflux capacity for those mutants.
evidence: This is based on SHAM sensitivity assays used as a proxy for glycerol transport.

claim: After 12 hr of CRK12 RNAi induction, CRK12 mRNA levels were reduced by 42% relative to uninduced controls.
source: At 12 hr of CRK12 RNAi induction with tetracycline, CRK12 mRNA levels were reduced by 42% (p<0.001) relative to uninduced controls as determined by qRT-PCR (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from qRT-PCR with statistical analysis.

claim: After 12 hr of CRK12 RNAi induction, pentamidine uptake was not significantly less than in the T. brucei 2T1 parental cells.
source: After 12 hr of CRK12 RNAi induction, pentamidine uptake was not significantly less than in the T. brucei 2T1 parental cells, whereas uptake of [3H]-suramin was (p=0.019, n = 5; Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is based on transport assays with statistical analysis.

claim: After 12 hr of CRK12 RNAi induction, uptake of [3H]-suramin was significantly reduced compared to control cells.
source: After 12 hr of CRK12 RNAi induction, pentamidine uptake was not significantly less than in the T. brucei 2T1 parental cells, whereas uptake of [3H]-suramin was (p=0.019, n = 5; Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is based on transport assays with statistical analysis.

claim: Pentamidine does not induce the internalisation and turnover of TbAQP2.
source: Quantification of the bands showed identical turnover rates with or without pentamidine present in the medium (Figure 6).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis of protein turnover.

claim: Ionophores including CCCP, nigericin and gramicidin strongly inhibited pentamidine uptake.
source: Although several ionophores, including CCCP, nigericin and gramicidin strongly inhibited pentamidine uptake, similar to what has been previously reported for transport processes in T. brucei that are linked to the protonmotive force (de Koning and Jarvis, 1997a; de Koning and Jarvis, 1997b; de Koning and Jarvis, 1998; de Koning et al., 1998), this is probably due to the inside-negative membrane potential of −125 mV (de Koning and Jarvis, 1997b) attracting the dicationic pentamidine.
evidence: This is based on transport assays with ionophores and cited literature.

claim: The membrane potential of T. b. brucei is −125 mV.
source: Although several ionophores, including CCCP, nigericin and gramicidin strongly inhibited pentamidine uptake, similar to what has been previously reported for transport processes in T. brucei that are linked to the protonmotive force (de Koning and Jarvis, 1997a; de Koning and Jarvis, 1997b; de Koning and Jarvis, 1998; de Koning et al., 1998), this is probably due to the inside-negative membrane potential of −125 mV (de Koning and Jarvis, 1997b) attracting the dicationic pentamidine.
evidence: This is a cited measurement from previous work.

claim: CCCP inhibits TbAQP2 directly with an IC50 of 20.7 ± 2.6 µM for glycerol uptake.
source: Indeed, CCCP inhibited uptake of (neutral) [3H]-glycerol in tbaqp1-2-3 null cells expressing TbAQP2-WT, with an IC50 of 20.7 ± 2.6 µM (n = 3) and inhibited [3H]-pentamidine uptake in the same cells with a similar IC50 (Figure 7D,E), showing CCCP to inhibit TbAQP2 directly, irrespective of effects on the membrane potential.
evidence: This is based on transport inhibition assays with quantitative measurements.

claim: Pentamidine inhibits [3H]-glycerol uptake with an EC50 of approximately 27.5 nM.
source: Figure 7D also shows that pentamidine, used as a control, inhibits [3H]-glycerol uptake with an EC50 value (Mean of 27.5 nM, n = 2) similar to the EC50 of pentamidine inhibiting uptake of [3H]-pentamidine.
evidence: This is based on transport inhibition assays.

claim: The docked position of pentamidine correctly identified its minimum free-energy binding site inside the TbAQP2 pore.
source: Figure 8A shows that the docked position of pentamidine correctly identified its minimum free-energy binding site inside the TbAQP2 pore.
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulations and free-energy calculations.

claim: Pentamidine adopts an extended state inside the TbAQP2 pore with inter-amidine lengths in the range 16.5–17 Å.
source: Pentamidine adopts an extended state inside the TbAQP2 pore, adapting its molecular shape to the narrow permeation channel; pentamidine binding poses display inter-amidine lengths in the range 16.5–17 Å.
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: Pentamidine can exit the TbAQP2 channel in either direction.
source: Importantly, our steered simulations reveal that pentamidine can exit the channel in either direction, and that unbinding on the route towards the cytoplasm occurs on a free-energy surface roughly symmetric to that towards the extracellular side.
evidence: This is based on steered molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: The voltage drop of −125 mV across the cytoplasmic membrane results in an overall inward attraction of ~22 kJ/mol for pentamidine.
source: The voltage drop of −125 mV across the cytoplasmic membrane of T. b. brucei (de Koning and Jarvis, 1997b), with a negative potential inside the cell, results in an overall inward attraction of ~22 kJ/mol (Figure 8A, arrow), that is exit from TbAQP2 into the cytoplasm is substantially more favourable for pentamidine than towards the extracellular side.
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics calculations incorporating membrane potential.

claim: The Vmax for HAPT-mediated pentamidine uptake is 0.0044 ± 0.0004 pmol(107 cells)−1 s−1.
source: The high affinity of the binding interaction leads to slow off-rates and a relatively low Vmax (0.0044 ± 0.0004 pmol(107 cells)−1 s−1) (de Koning, 2001a).
evidence: This is a cited quantitative measurement from previous work.

claim: Pentamidine analogues featuring 5–7 methylene units displayed submicromolar binding affinities.
source: Pentamidine analogues featuring 5–7 units displayed submicromolar binding affinities (5 > 6 > 7), while fewer (3-4) or more (8) only conveyed low micromolar binding affinity, equivalent to a decrease in Gibbs free energy of binding (ΔG0) from 10.2 to 13.0 kJ/mol (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays with pentamidine analogues.

claim: Replacement of the ether oxygens with S or NH resulted in δ(ΔG0) of 10.0 and 12.9 kJ/mol, respectively.
source: Replacement of the ether oxygens with S or NH, analogues RT-48 and RT-50, respectively (Table 1) resulted in δ(ΔG0) of 10.0 and 12.9 kJ/mol, respectively, indicating that the ether oxygens potentially act as H-bond acceptors: the NH group serves only as an H-bond donor, as its lone pair is conjugated with the aromatic system, and the sulphur mimics an aromatic NH (Beno et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays with pentamidine analogues and cited literature.

claim: The sulfone analogue (RT-49) displayed no binding affinity.
source: The sulfone analogue (RT-49), which introduces a dihedral angle of 180° between the benzamidine and the linker (Brameld et al., 2008), displayed no binding affinity.
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays with cited structural information.

claim: Replacement of the middle methylene unit of pentamidine with an isosteric oxygen results in a remarkable drop in binding affinity (δ(ΔG0)=15.3 kJ/mol).
source: Replacement of the middle methylene unit of pentamidine with an isosteric oxygen (ethylene glycol derivative DB1699, Table 1) results in a less flexible linker and a remarkable drop in binding affinity (δ(ΔG0)=15.3 kJ/mol).
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays with pentamidine analogues.

claim: Both amidines contribute to high affinity binding of pentamidine to TbAQP2.
source: Matched-molecular pair analysis of non-symmetric analogues identified that both amidines contribute to high affinity binding (compare pairs pentamidine/RT-36 and pentamidine/CHI/1/72/1; Table 1).
evidence: This is based on structure-activity relationship analysis of inhibition data.

claim: Removal of an H-bond donor leads to a loss in ΔG0 > 10 kJ/mol.
source: Removal of an H-bond donor (as in CHI/1/72/1) leads to a loss in ΔG0 > 10 kJ/mol.
evidence: This is based on structure-activity relationship analysis.

claim: Stilbamidine and the short-linker analogues FR39 and CRMI8 displayed low binding affinity.
source: Stilbamidine and the short-linker analogues FR39 and CRMI8 (Ríos Martínez et al., 2015) displayed low binding affinity (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays.

claim: Diminazene displayed a Ki of 63 µM for TbAQP2.
source: Diminazene also displayed similar low affinity (Ki = 63 µM), and [3H]-diminazene uptake can only just be detected in procyclic T. b. brucei, that is in the absence of the TbAT1/P2 transporter (Teka et al., 2011), potentially indicating a minimal uptake via HAPT1.
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays and cited transport data.

claim: DB75 (furamidine) displayed low affinity for TbAQP2.
source: DB75 (furamidine) likewise displayed low affinity (Table 2) and is only internalised by TbAT1/P2 (Ward et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays and cited transport data.

claim: DB607 and DB960 display a somewhat higher affinity than DB75 for TbAQP2.
source: Thus, DB607 (methoxy for amidine) and DB960 (N-methyl benzimidazole for benzamidine) display a somewhat higher affinity than DB75, although the fixed angle was unchanged.
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays and structural comparison.

claim: DB994 shows a complete loss of binding affinity with a Ki of 167 ± 20 µM.
source: Introduction of a pyridine-N in the ortho-position with respect to the amidine functionality (DB994), dramatically reduces the pKa of the amidine moiety (Wang et al., 2010), resulting in a complete loss of binding affinity (Ki = 167 ± 20 µM), while this was not observed for the corresponding meta-pyridine derivative (DB829).
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays with cited structural information.

claim: DB914 (difuran spacer) resulted in a high affinity binder with Ki = 0.073 µM.
source: A difuran spacer (DB914) resulted in a high affinity binder (Ki = 0.073 µM) because the two furans orient themselves in a trans conformation, resulting in a near-linear molecule.
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays with structural interpretation.

claim: Isometamidium inhibited HAPT1-mediated [3H]-pentamidine uptake with a Ki of 3.5 µM.
source: The important veterinary trypanocide isometamidium, a hybrid of the phenanthridine ethidium and the diamidine diminazene, inhibited HAPT1-mediated [3H]-pentamidine uptake with a Ki of only 3.5 µM (Supplementary file 1), most probably through an interaction with its benzamidine moiety, as ethidium displayed virtually no affinity (Ki = 97 µM).
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays.

claim: There is no evidence that HAPT1/AQP2 is able to transport isometamidium.
source: However, we found no evidence that HAPT1/AQP2 is able to transport the bulky isometamidium molecule. For instance, the 2T1, tbaqp2 null, TbAQP2 expressed in tbaqp2 null, and the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null strains displayed statistically identical EC50 values for isometamidium (112 ± 12 nM, 103 ± 14 nM, 98 ± 24 nM and 95 ± 12 nM, respectively; p>0.05, Student's unpaired t-test), and the EC50 values for ethidium were also identical for each of these strains (1.32 ± 0.07 µM, 1.39 ± 0.08 µM, 1.35 ± 0.11 µM and 1.38 ± 0.14 µM, respectively).
evidence: This is based on drug sensitivity assays across multiple cell lines.

claim: Phloretin displayed a Ki of 1.76 µM for HAPT1/TbAQP2.
source: Phloretin, which inhibits human AQP9 and AQP3 (Geng et al., 2017),47 displayed a Ki of 1.76 µM for HAPT1/TbAQP2.
evidence: This is based on inhibition assays with cited information about phloretin's activity on human aquaporins.

claim: There is a poor correlation (r2 = 0.039) between HAPT1 binding affinity and the level of resistance in the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null strain.
source: We observed a poor correlation between HAPT1 binding affinity and the level of resistance in the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null strain (r2 = 0.039, Figure 9—figure supplement 1; n = 30), with many inhibitors, even those with high affinity, not displaying any significant resistance in the null line.
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis of binding and resistance data.

claim: Many HAPT1 inhibitors do not show resistance in the tbaqp2/tbaqp3 null line, indicating they are not transported by TbAQP2.
source: This indicates that many of these compounds inhibit HAPT1/TbAQP2 but are not transported by it.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lack of correlation between binding and resistance.

claim: No modification in any part of pentamidine improved affinity for TbAQP2.
source: No modification in any part of pentamidine improved affinity for TbAQP2, but virtually every modification resulted in a significant loss of binding activity (a similar analysis with melaminophenyl arsenicals was impossible for lack of the required organo-arsenicals).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the structure-activity relationship study.

claim: At least both amidine groups and one or both ether oxygens are involved in interactions with AQP2.
source: The results clearly demonstrate that at least both amidine groups and one or both ether oxygens are involved in interactions with AQP2, the sum of which adds up to the unusually high binding energy for this substrate-transporter pair (ΔG0 = −42.6 kJ/mol).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structure-activity relationship study.

claim: The Gibbs free energy of interaction between pentamidine and TbAQP2 is ΔG0 = −42.6 kJ/mol.
source: The results clearly demonstrate that at least both amidine groups and one or both ether oxygens are involved in interactions with AQP2, the sum of which adds up to the unusually high binding energy for this substrate-transporter pair (ΔG0 = −42.6 kJ/mol).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement cited from previous work.

claim: TbAQP2 has evolved by positive selection to remove all main constriction points, resulting in an unprecedentedly enlarged pore size.
source: TbAQP2 has evolved, apparently by positive selection given the high dN/dS ratio, to remove all main constriction points, including the aromatic amino acids and the cationic arginine of the ar/R selectivity filter, and the NPA/NPA motif, resulting in an unprecedentedly enlarged pore size (Baker et al., 2012; Munday et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on phylogenetic analysis and cited structural studies.

claim: The rate of endocytosis in bloodstream trypanosomes is much higher than in the procyclic lifecycle forms.
source: For instance, the rate of endocytosis in bloodstream trypanosomes is much higher than in the procyclic lifecycle forms (Langreth and Balber, 1975; Zoltner et al., 2016), yet the rate of HAPT-mediated [3H]-pentamidine uptake in procyclics is ~10 fold higher than in bloodstream forms (de Koning, 2001a; Teka et al., 2011), despite the level of TbAQP2 expression being similar in both cases (Siegel et al., 2010; Jensen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on cited literature comparing endocytosis and transport rates.

claim: The rate of HAPT-mediated [3H]-pentamidine uptake in procyclics is ~10 fold higher than in bloodstream forms.
source: For instance, the rate of endocytosis in bloodstream trypanosomes is much higher than in the procyclic lifecycle forms (Langreth and Balber, 1975; Zoltner et al., 2016), yet the rate of HAPT-mediated [3H]-pentamidine uptake in procyclics is ~10 fold higher than in bloodstream forms (de Koning, 2001a; Teka et al., 2011), despite the level of TbAQP2 expression being similar in both cases (Siegel et al., 2010; Jensen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on cited transport measurements.

claim: The level of TbAQP2 expression is similar in bloodstream and procyclic forms.
source: For instance, the rate of endocytosis in bloodstream trypanosomes is much higher than in the procyclic lifecycle forms (Langreth and Balber, 1975; Zoltner et al., 2016), yet the rate of HAPT-mediated [3H]-pentamidine uptake in procyclics is ~10 fold higher than in bloodstream forms (de Koning, 2001a; Teka et al., 2011), despite the level of TbAQP2 expression being similar in both cases (Siegel et al., 2010; Jensen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on cited expression studies.

claim: In procyclic cells, TbAQP2 is spread out over the cell surface.
source: Moreover, in procyclic cells TbAQP2 is spread out over the cell surface (Baker et al., 2012) but endocytosis happens exclusively in the flagellar pocket (Field and Carrington, 2009) (which is 3-fold smaller in procyclic than in bloodstream forms [Demmel et al., 2014]), as the pellicular microtubule networks below the plasma membrane prevent endocytosis (Zoltner et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on cited localization studies.

claim: Endocytosis happens exclusively in the flagellar pocket in trypanosomes.

claim: Expression of TbAQP2 in Leishmania mexicana promastigotes produced a rate of [3H]-pentamidine uptake more than 10-fold higher than observed in T. brucei BSF.
source: Similarly, the expression of TbAQP2 in Leishmania mexicana promastigotes produced a rate of [3H]-pentamidine uptake more than 10-fold higher than observed in T. brucei BSF (Munday et al., 2014), despite these cells also having a low endocytosis rate (Langreth and Balber, 1975).
evidence: This is based on cited transport measurements in heterologous expression.

claim: The experimental Vmax for HAPT-mediated pentamidine uptake in T. brucei BSF is 9.5 × 10^5 molecules/cell/h.
source: The experimental Vmax for HAPT-mediated pentamidine uptake in T. brucei BSF and procyclics (de Koning, 2001a) can be expressed as 9.5 × 105 and 8.5 × 106 molecules/cell/h, respectively; given a 1:1 stoichiometry for AQP2:pentamidine the endocytosis model would require the internalisation and recycling of as many units of TbAQP2 and this seems unlikely, especially in procyclic cells, as even in BSF the half-life time for TbAQP2 turnover is >4 hr (Quintana et al., 2020) and procyclic cells have a lower endocytosis rate and cannot easily internalise the aquaporins spread over the cell surface, as discussed above.

source: Furthermore, the Gibbs free energy of −42 kJ/mol for the pentamidine/AQP2 interaction (de Koning, 2001a; Zoltner et al., 2016) is highly unlikely to be the result of the one interaction between one terminal amidine and Asp265 as required in the endocytosis model (Song et al., 2016).

claim: A double H-bond interaction of Asp140 with the N1(H)/C(6)NH2 motif of adenosine or with one amidine of pentamidine in TbAT1 is estimated to contribute only ~16 kJ/mol to the total ΔG0.
source: For the TbAT1 transporter, a double H-bond interaction of Asp140 with the N1(H)/C(6)NH2 motif of adenosine or with one amidine of pentamidine (Munday et al., 2015b) is estimated to contribute only ~16 kJ/mol to the total ΔG0 of −34.5 kJ/mol for adenosine (−36.7 kJ/mol, pentamidine) (de Koning and Jarvis, 1999).

claim: The combined evidence strongly suggests that pentamidine is not taken up by endocytosis.

claim: The primary entry of pentamidine and melarsoprol into T. brucei spp. is through the unusually large pore of TbAQP2.
source: Altogether, we conclude that the primary entry of the sleeping sickness drugs pentamidine and melarsoprol into T. brucei spp. is through the unusually large pore of TbAQP2, rendering the parasite extraordinarily sensitive to the drugs (compare Leishmania mexicana [Munday et al., 2014]).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on all presented evidence.
